summary: The paper presents a tour-de-force mathematical and computational breakthrough in proving rapid mixing of quantum Gibbs samplers beyond the spectral gap for non-commuting Hamiltonian systems. By introducing the basis-independent Quantum Christoffel Operator, deriving exact piecewise-logarithmic mixing laws via upper-convex-hull integration, and establishing zero-floating-point-trust exact-Q LDL^T PSD certificates backed by a zero-dependency Lean 4 formalization (0 sorry), the work achieves exemplary standards of rigor, correctness, and reproducibility. Comprehensive numerical benchmarks on non-commuting TFIM and XXZ spin chains demonstrate substantial speedups (up to 3.30x) over naive spectral gap bounds, while scaling gracefully to n = 1,000 qubits.
weaknesses: The synthesis script estimates input Frobenius radii against floating-point eigh(H) outputs, requiring interval-certified eigensolvers for end-to-end exact provenance from H without synthesis-stage approximations.
